articles.title: SIR officers recall notice, go to Padma Shri awardee Harekala’s house, fix gaps
articles.summary: Padma Shri awardee Harekala Hajabba was mistakenly issued an Election Commission notice over a voter list name mismatch; officials later corrected it and withdrew notice.
articles.body: MANGALURU: Padma Shri awardee Harekala Hajabba received a notice from the Election Commission Monday directing him to appear before the assistant electoral registration officer (AERO) Friday. However, after officials realised the error, the tahsildar and village assistant visited the 70-year-old man’s house, made the necessary corrections and spared him a trip to the AERO’s office.Ashwini, village assistant of Harekala gram panchayat, who visited Hajabba’s house, said the notice was generated because his name had earlier been registered as ‘Hajabba’ and was later changed to ‘Harekala Hajabba’.“This spelling mismatch led to the voter being placed in the logical discrepancy category. Booth-level officers had clear instructions to resolve discrepancies involving VIPs immediately, without issuing notices. However, due to an oversight, a notice was served on the Padma Shri awardee,” Ashwini said, expressing regret.The discrepancy led to a notice being issued to Hajabba, a voter from Ramakrishna High School, New Padpu, in Harekala village, which falls under the Mangaluru constituency represented by health minister UT Khader.Hajabba told TOI that the booth-level officer had asked him to appear with the necessary documents to rectify the error in the voter list.“As per the notice, I was supposed to appear before the AERO on Friday. However, officials visited my house and collected the documents,” he said.The notice was withdrawn within hours and officials rectified the error after collecting the necessary documents. Ashwini said the discrepancy had been resolved at the official level.Hajabba, who sold oranges and was deeply pained by his lack of access to education, took up the challenge of building a school in Harekala in 1995. He worked to secure land and obtain approval from the education department.His dream became a reality in 1999 when the Dakshina Kannada zilla panchayat sanctioned the school. The Dakshina Kannada Zilla Panchayat Lower Primary School, popularly known as ‘Hajabba avara Shale’, initially functioned out of a madrassa. Later, Hajabba built classrooms on 40 cents of land sanctioned by the district administration. The school was subsequently upgraded into a pre-university college. articles.title: Attempt to make example out of Aakriti: Official excesses will make UP a Orwellian dystopia, warns HC
articles.summary: Allahabad HC quashes NSA detention of DU activist Akriti Chaudhary, cites Article 21 violation, slams Noida DM, orders Rs 5 lakh compensation recovered from officials.
articles.body: PRAYAGRAJ: In a strongly worded order giving the detailed reasons for quashing the National Security Act (NSA) detention of Delhi University student activist Akriti Chaudhary, the Allahabad high court cautioned that errant bureaucrats could reduce Uttar Pradesh to an "Orwellian dystopia" and reminded civil servants that their loyalty lies with the Constitution and not the political executive.The 15-page order, made public days after the court quashed the NSA detention and awarded Rs 5 lakh compensation to Chaudhary on Sept 2, contains sharp criticism of the Gautam Budh Nagar administration and police for invoking the stringent preventive detention law against a student activist without adequate material.A division bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev observed that bureaucrats and police officers enjoy immense powers because they are entrusted with protecting the constitutional rights, dignity and welfare of citizens. "They must remember that their loyalty is towards the Constitution and not the political executive," the court said.Warning against abuse of authority, the bench observed that when officials disregard their constitutional oath, they risk being perceived as "an oppressive vestige of the British Empire", creating conditions for civil unrest. "It shall not be long before the errant in the bureaucracy reduce the State of Uttar Pradesh to an Orwellian Dystopia," the court remarked.The bench was particularly critical of Gautam Budh Nagar DM Medha Roopam, who had approved the NSA detention. It held that where the police dossier contained only allegations and no credible supporting material, the district magistrate was expected to scrutinise the records threadbare before invoking the extraordinary powers available under the NSA."The conduct of the district magistrate, Gautam Budh Nagar, who passed the impugned order, is worthy of derision," the court observed.Chaudhary, a Delhi University graduate and activist, was booked following labour protests in Noida earlier this year. Examining the WhatsApp chats, videos and other material relied upon by the state, the court repeatedly sought evidence showing that she had incited violence, rioting, arson or destruction of property. According to the order, the state was unable to point to any such material.Instead, the bench found that the videos merely showed people gathering to demand better wages and humane working conditions. It noted that Chaudhary was a student activist with no criminal antecedents and there was nothing on record to suggest she had encouraged violence.The court went on to observe that the circumstances indicated an attempt to make an example out of Chaudhary in order to deter others from exercising their constitutional right to freedom of speech and expression in support of labourers.The judges also found inconsistencies in the state's version of Chaudhary's arrest. While she claimed she was picked up from Botanical Garden Metro Station on April 11, the state maintained she was arrested on April 12. Examining documents placed on record, the court concluded that a notice issued under Section 130 of the BNSS appeared to have been prepared after her arrest and described the exercise as a "sham".The bench underscored that detention under the NSA is an exceptional measure and cannot become a substitute for ordinary criminal law. It described the grounds of detention as "repetitive, speculative and only opinion-based", lacking supporting evidence."The extraordinary power resulting in incarceration cannot be exercised lightly on the basis of surmises, biases, conjectures and opinions," the court said.Making broader observations on democratic freedoms, the court held that freedom of speech and expression includes the right of citizens to gather peacefully in public spaces and agitate for their rights. Preventing such assemblies merely on the assumption that they may result in a breach of peace would amount to "throwing the baby out with the bath water", it said.The HC also directed that its displeasure against the district magistrate and police officers involved in preparing the NSA dossier be recorded in their service records.Stay updated with the latest Prayagraj news. articles.title: Aspiring CA, 18, dies in Delhi PG collapse hours after Rakhi at home in MP; family donates corneas
articles.summary: Delhi Satya Niketan building collapse kills four students; families identify bodies at AIIMS as dreams of IAS, CA and studies are cut short.
articles.body: Akshat Yadav (18)A mole on his neck and a mark left by a surgery on his right leg helped Akshat’s mother Sweta identify his body at AIIMS Monday.Akshat dreamt of becoming an IAS officer and making his parents proud. However, the dream was crushed beneath the rubble of the collapsed Satya Niketan building when the body of the second-year BCom (Hons) student at PGDAV College was pulled out at 7 am Monday.Akshat had been living in Delhi for the past two years and was a boarder at the PG accommodation for nearly a year. He lived on the first floor of the building and paid Rs 18,000 a month as rent. He returned to the city from his hometown in MP just two days before the incident after celebrating Raksha Bandhan.His cousin, Deepankar, who helped him find the accommodation, said, “I told Akshat to shift to Mayur Vihar, but he did not. He told me that it was only a matter of one year and that it would easily pass,” Deepankar said.Akshat’s family rushed to the spot after learning about the collapse. Just hours before the tragedy, on Sunday morning, Akshat had spoken to his parents over a video call. “Everything was fine,” Deepankar said.Hours later, the family was desperately searching for him in the rubble. Akshat’s wallet was found at the spot, helping the family establish that he was among those trapped in the debris. His body was later identified at AIIMS mortuary.His neighbour, Vijay Kumar Rajak, said Akshat was good at studies. “He mostly kept to himself and focused on his studies,” Rajak said.At AIIMS, Akshat’s younger sister wept inconsolably as the family struggled to come to terms with the loss of a young man whose ambitions and dreams were cut short.Yuvraj Soni (20)For Yuvraj’s relatives, the tragedy came as a double blow. Not only did they lose him, but his father, Kanhaiya, had to be hospitalised after being told that his son was critical. The family has not yet told Kanhiaya, who runs a medical store in Chhattisgarh, that Yuvraj is no more, fearing that the news is likely to worsen his condition.Yuvraj was speaking to his friend Gunjan on the phone when the building collapsed. The call suddenly disconnected, and Gunjan received no response despite repeatedly trying to contact him.A native of Chhattisgarh, Yuvraj was a BCom (Hons) student at Motilal Nehru College and was known to his friends and acquaintances as quiet and studious. He shifted to the fourth floor of the PG accommodation just a week before tragedy struck Sunday, his cousin said.On receiving information about the building collapse, Yuvraj’s relatives rushed to Delhi and waited anxiously as rescue teams cleared the debris. Through the long hours of the search, they continued to hope that Yuvraj would survive. Their hope, however, was dashed when his body was pulled out.Arpit Jaj (18)Arpit’s family has decided to donate his corneas, hoping that even in death, he could help someone else regain their sight.The second-year BCom student, who aspired to become a chartered accountant, returned to his PG at 8am Sunday after celebrating Raksha Bandhan and Janmashtami with his family in MP’s Dewas, his friend Mayank said. Just a few hours later, the building turned into a death trap.Initially, Arpit’s family believed he was asleep when his mother’s calls went unanswered. Later, the family was informed about the incident and rushed to the spot, but it was all over by then. His body was identified at 6 pm.Arpit’s mother was seen weeping inconsolably at AIIMS, repeatedly asking why no one stopped him from returning to Delhi.Pawan Kumar (17)A last-minute change in plans proved fatal for this native of UP’s Auraiya. Pawan had planned to visit his cousin Saturday and stay there till Sunday, but decided against. Hours later, he was trapped in the collapsed building.Pawan, who has four sister, was pursuing computer science with mathematics at Motilal Nehru College. His father is a retired veterinary doctor. His cousin, Dhiraj, said the PG was in a dilapidated condition.As soon as Pawan’s relatives heard about the collapse, they rushed to the spot and waited anxiously as rescue teams searched through the rubble. For several hours, they held onto the hope that he had survived as people at the site told them that some trapped residents had been rescued. “Many people said Pawan had been rescued and he was alive,” Dhiraj said.The family continued waiting for confirmation, clinging to every piece of information coming from the rescue site. Just after 10pm, their hopes were dashed when they learnt that Pawan had died. At the hospital, his father looked devastated, struggling to come to terms with the catastrophic loss.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Satya Niketan building collapse: DU students seek hostels, safety steps, accountability
articles.summary: DU students protest after Satya Niketan building collapse near South Campus, demanding accountability, compensation, more hostels, and safety audits of PGs.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Satya Niketan building collapse, just a few steps from Delhi University’s South Campus, has left students worried about where they should stay and how.Monday, students marched from the arts faculty to the VC’s office, holding up banners that said, “200 acres of land is lying vacant, yet no hostel for students.” Another read, “Provide accommodation to students. It is our right.”Students’ organisations such as Disha, All India Democratic Students Organisation (AIDSO), Students Federation of India (SFI) and Krantanikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS) also participated in the march. Anger over the lack of affordable and safe accommodation is what brought the students out to the protest.For Himantri, the tragedy hit close to home. Her hostel is next to the building that collapsed. “It is frightening to see something like this happen next door. It is not as if students do not pay rent. Many of us are paying as much as Rs 20,000 for a room, yet our lives remain at risk. Even my building is very old. This is not just about what happened to these students. We need to ensure no one else suffers the same fate,” she said.Tarunima, who lives with her family in Delhi, said she joined the march out of concern for her friends who live in paying guest acommodations or PGs. “My friend lives in a PG and it is pathetic... It feels so wrong that so many students have no safe option,” she said.Chiranshu, another protester, said students were demanding immediate compensation for the victims and a serious rethink of the university’s hostel policy. “This is not the first such incident. Hostels are available to only around 3.5% of students. Most of them are meant for boys, while some hostels are also closed. Where are the rest of the students supposed to go?” he said.Students alleged that the Satya Niketan tragedy reflected a larger failure of enforcement, with illegal construction, alleged collusion among landlords, builders and authorities, and violations of safety norms putting lives at risk. For them, however, the problem begins much earlier. Why are DU students being pushed into expensive PGs and flats in the first place?They said areas such as Kamla Nagar, Vijay Nagar and Satya Niketan have become hubs for students looking for accommodation, often leaving students dependent on ageing or poorly maintained buildings.They demanded that DU immediately reopen hostels that have remained closed for years and use its available land to build more accommodation. They also called for affordable student housing and regular safety audits of buildings in student-dominated areas.The Satya Niketan collapse has triggered protests beyond the campus. ABVP held a late-night protest Sunday and entered the MCD office, demanding the commissioner’s resignation.On Monday, ABVP held protests and sit-ins across several Delhi University colleges, demanding accountability and stronger student safety measures. Demonstrations were held at Hansraj College, Hindu College, Kirori Mal College, Ramjas College, Shaheed Bhagat Singh College and several other campuses. The ABVP demanded a high-level probe into the building collapse, strict action against negligent PG operators, building owners and officials, and immediate structural and safety audits.ABVP national general secretary Dr Virendra Singh Solanki said: “No student in Delhi should ever risk his life by living in an unsafe building.”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Angry MPSC aspirants warn of Jantar Mantar-like stir if govt fails to act in 3 days
articles.summary: MPSC aspirants protest across Maharashtra over alleged drug inspector exam paper leak, seeking chairman’s resignation, probe, report release; warn bigger stir in 3 days.
articles.body: PUNE: Hundreds of aspirants took to the streets across Maharashtra on Monday, demanding the resignation of Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) chairman and secretary, a high-level probe into the alleged irregularities in the commission’s drug inspector examination case and that the preliminary inquiry report submitted by Mumbai crime branch be made public.The protesters warned of a Jantar Mantar-like protest if the state govt did not act on their demands in three days. The agitation came in the wake of the alleged paper leak in the MPSC Drug Inspector examination and the arrest of officials linked to the commission’s confidential section.Carrying placards and raising slogans in Pune, the protesters marched from Omkareshwar Chowk to the collectorate, halting traffic on several arterial roads. In Kolhapur, the agitators marched under the umbrella of ‘All Competitive Exams Students Action Committee’ from Dasara Chowk to the collectorate.Protesters sat on the road outside Pune collectorate while a delegation submitted a memorandum to the district administration.“We have studied for years, but are forced to stand on the roads with placards. If govt does not accept our demands, we will intensify the agitation. Our futures cannot be put at risk because of irregularities in the examination system,” Nitin Andhale, student representative and organiser of the protest, said.The aspirants also demanded a forensic audit of all MPSC examinations conducted during the tenure of officials working in the commission’s confidential section who are facing scrutiny in the paper leak case and an inquiry into their service records, promotions and the criteria used for their appointments and promotions.They also want an investigation into the suspected network involved in the paper leak, a scrutiny of financial transactions, call records, digital evidence and the contact network of the suspects.Aspirant Sumit Jadhav said, “We want an independent inquiry into doubts surrounding the results of other MPSC examinations. We need an explanation from the commission in eight days on objections raised by candidates regarding the Group B examination and a govt inquiry into whether any irregularity had occurred.”Protester Asmita Kale said students also want an inquiry into errors noticed during evaluation of descriptive answer sheets for State Services Main Examination 2025 and agriculture services examination and into alleged irregularities in the departmental examinations conducted by the state excise department and for police sub-inspectors.Youth Congress leader Akshay Jain said young people should be holding question papers not protest placards. “We need transparency, accountability and action against those responsible,” he said. Others said they would press for regular public updates on the investigation.MPSC chairman Vivek Bhimanwar said his statement on Sept 2, 2026 clarified that the drug inspector exam paper leak happened before he joined yet repeated allegations are being made against him about it.He said the commission filed a police complaint immediately and the investigation is underway. The commission and the govt have formed high-level committees and started consultations with students, parents and teachers at the divisional level.Bhimanwar said he was deeply distressed by the continued personal and politically motivated allegations against him. He added that he introduced several reforms in MPSC and conducted 84 examinations, including eight competitive examinations and 76 screening examinations for direct recruitment.Several improvements made it possible to declare results between 18 and 21 days from the time govt sought recruitment and plans are to declare other results within a month.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news. articles.title: Kanpur engineer detained in Moscow; embassy seeks consular access
articles.summary: Kanpur engineer Chandan Gupta detained in Moscow; Indian Embassy seeks consular access as wife appeals for intervention amid fears of forced military enlistment.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Soon after a Kanpur-based engineer working in Moscow was reportedly detained by Russian police, prompting his wife to appeal to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath for his release and safe return to India, the Indian Embassy in Russia sought consular access.Chandan Gupta, 40, had travelled to Russia with his family on a work visa and is working with a Noida-based Indian company. His wife, Sneha, has released a video seeking govt intervention, claiming that Russian police took her husband away from their residence late Sunday.Taking note of Sneha’s video, the Indian Embassy posted on X: “We have seen a social media post by an Indian national regarding her husband. We are in touch with her and the local authorities in the matter. As per law enforcement authorities, it is a legal matter and they are looking into it. The Embassy has also sought consular access.”The embassy issued the statement soon after Chandan’s wife expressed fears that he could be pressured into joining the Russian military. “I am afraid that my husband may be sent to the Russian Army forcibly,” she said, appealing to the authorities to ensure his safety.There is no independent confirmation so far that Chandan has been recruited or is being sent to the Russian military.Sneha said she is currently in Moscow with their 10-year-old child and is finding it difficult to understand and navigate the situation as she does not speak Russian.In her video appeal of a little over one minute, Sneha claimed Russian police arrived at around 12.30 am and took Chandan with them. She claimed that she was subsequently informed that her husband had been kept in custody. According to her, Chandan had not committed any act that warranted his detention, and she has not been given adequate information about the circumstances surrounding his arrest.However, reports reaching India said Chandan was detained along with a friend, Ashish, around 11.30 pm (local time) on Sept 5 from Moscow’s Red Square premises on charges of drunkenness and allegedly breaking the glass of a nearby ambulance. “They are currently detained at the Baumanskaya police station in Moscow. The embassy has raised the matter with the local authorities and requested their release. Meanwhile, consular access has also been sought,” sources said.According to her, officials have told her that Chandan would be released, but she said she has not received a concrete update about when or under what circumstances he would be set free.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: Yemen conflict widens: Houthis claim strikes on Saudi airport, air base and Aramco sites
articles.summary: Middle East News: Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis said on September 8 that they had launched missiles and drones at Abha International Airport, King Khalid air base and Ara.
articles.body: Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis said on September 8 that they had launched missiles and drones at Abha International Airport, King Khalid air base and Aramco facilities in Abha and Jizan.“Yemeni drones and missiles pound the Saudi enemy,” Houthi media outlet Ansarollah said on Telegram. Another Ansarollah post named the airport, military base and oil facilities among the targets.Houthi attacks follow September 7 escalationThe Saudi-led coalition said on September 7 that 73 people were injured in Houthi attacks on civilian and economic sites. The attacks affected Abha, Khamis Mushait, Najran and Jazan, and the coalition said it would respond firmly, according to Reuters.On the same day, the Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of air strikes and cruise missile attacks in Jawf, Al-Bayda, Marib and Taiz. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the alleged Saudi attacks “will not go unanswered or unpunished”. Saudi Arabia did not publicly confirm the Houthi allegations.One of the alleged Saudi strikes hit a prison in Al-Hazm, Jawf province, according to Houthi media. The Houthi-run health ministry initially reported seven deaths, including a child, and at least seven injuries, according to the Associated Press. Separately, Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces said their own warplanes struck Houthi positions on September 7.Houthi official puts prison toll at 11By September 8, Jawf civil defence chief Hassan Saboula put the Houthi-reported prison death toll at 11 and said 20 inmates remained missing beneath the rubble, according to the Houthi-run Al-Masirah. Houthi-affiliated Saba said a child visiting the facility was among those killed.Fighting intensifies near Bab al-MandabThe latest exchange comes amid fighting near Yemen’s Red Sea coast. More than 300 people have been killed in the recent clashes, while hundreds of families have been forced from their homes. The Houthis are pressing an offensive for territory along the Bab al-Mandab Strait.Bab al-Mandab connects the Gulf of Aden with the Red Sea, which leads north to the Suez Canal. The route has gained importance for Saudi crude shipments as Iran’s blockade restricts traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Liverpool weather: Heavy rain and cooler temperatures expected Tuesday, September 8, 2026
articles.summary: UK News: Liverpool residents are bracing for a wet and cooler start to the week as heavy rain is forecast for Tuesday, September 8, 2026. This significant shif.
articles.body: Liverpool residents are bracing for a wet and cooler start to the week as heavy rain is forecast for Tuesday, September 8, 2026. This significant shift from recent pleasant weather will necessitate adjustments to daily routines, with high humidity and blustery winds expected. The latter half of the week and the weekend are predicted to bring improving conditions with sunny intervals and warmer temperatures.Tuesday's Detailed ForecastHeavy rain is set to dominate Tuesday, September 8, 2026, in Liverpool. The forecast indicates a high likelihood of significant precipitation, making it a wet and potentially disruptive day. Temperatures will be cooler, with a maximum expected around 18°C and a low of 11°C. The average temperature for the day is predicted to be 14.5°C.Humidity levels are expected to be high, reaching up to 96%. This will contribute to the damp feeling throughout the day. Wind speeds could reach up to 45.06 kph, adding to the blustery conditions.Advice for ResidentsGiven the forecast for heavy rain and high humidity, it is strongly advised that residents carry umbrellas and wear waterproof footwear. Outdoor plans may need to be reconsidered or adapted to account for the wet weather. Commuters should allow for extra travel time due to potentially slippery roads and reduced visibility. Indoor activities are likely to be the most comfortable option for much of the day.Looking Ahead: The Week's OutlookLooking ahead, the weather is expected to improve gradually over the coming week. While Tuesday will be wet, Wednesday, September 9, is forecast to bring sunny intervals. Temperatures will reach up to 19°C with a low of 9°C.This trend of mixed conditions is set to continue. Overcast skies are expected on Thursday, September 10, and Friday, September 11. Temperatures will climb during this period, with highs reaching 19°C and 21°C respectively.The weekend appears to offer more pleasant weather. Sunny intervals are predicted for Saturday, September 12, and Sunday, September 13. Highs are expected to be around 20°C and 21°C. The latter half of the week will see a warming trend. articles.title: Who was Chongtham Vikram, Manipuri musician killed in Delhi attack; cousin of BAFTA-winning ‘Boong’ director
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Chongtham Vikram Singh, a 55-year-old Manipuri musician, was allegedly beaten to death outside his Delhi home on Sunday night after he went.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Chongtham Vikram Singh, a 55-year-old Manipuri musician, was allegedly beaten to death outside his Delhi home on Sunday night after he went downstairs to object to a group of men creating a ruckus.Who was Chongtham Vikram Singh?Singh was a gifted guitarist who had spent decades making music his language.He played lead guitar for several bands in Manipur before moving to Delhi nearly 20 years ago, where he built a life around his passion for music.A resident of Thangmeiband Lourung Purel Leikai in Imphal West, Singh later established a music school in Delhi, mentored students from home and also taught at the Delhi School of Music.His musical journey included the Rock'n'Roots project, through which he collaborated with Rajasthani folk singer Mame Khan. He also worked with several other renowned musicians for cultural shows and concerts.Singh came from a family with a strong musical legacy. His mother, 86-year-old Chongtham Ongbi Kamala Devi, is a renowned classical and modern Manipuri singer.Singh was also a cousin of Lakshmipriya Devi, director of Boong, India's first BAFTA Award-winning film.He is survived by his wife, Jyotsana, 54, and their 20-year-old son, Yaiphaba. Jyotsana works as a senior consultant with an MNC, while Yaiphaba is a law student.What happened on Sunday night?According to Singh's family, a group of eight men, allegedly intoxicated, were creating a ruckus outside his home around 11pm. Singh went downstairs to ask them to stop.A few minutes later, his family heard him banging on the door and shouting, "Thong hango! Thong hango!" (open the door, open the door).His son, Yaiphaba, found him in a semi-conscious state with his T-shirt ripped apart. He was rushed to Holy Family Hospital, where doctors found his blood pressure had fallen below 50mm Hg. His condition was too critical for surgery and he died around 6.30am on Monday.Talking to TOI from Imphal, Singh's brother Vivek said the family had not yet told their 96-year-old father, Dr Chongtham Birendra Singh, about the death, fearing he would not be able to bear the loss. His mother, he said, was inconsolable.Friends remembered Singh as a gentle and accomplished musician who remained deeply passionate about his craft.Protest over musician's deathManipuri associations in Delhi said that although the postmortem had been completed, they did not want Singh's body to be sent to Manipur until justice was done."Once the last rites are over, only the family bears the loss, and the incident fades into oblivion," a Manipuri activist in Delhi said.Northeast student groups, friends and family members also staged a protest outside Sunlight Colony police station, demanding justice in the case.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: DMK MLAs evicted from TN assembly after ruckus over CM Vijay's remarks
articles.summary: India News: DMK legislators were bundled out of the Tamil Nadu assembly on Tuesday following intense protests demanding the expunging of Chief Minister C Joseph V.
articles.body: DMK legislators were bundled out of the Tamil Nadu assembly on Tuesday following intense protests demanding the expunging of Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s remarks regarding former Chief Minister M Karunanidhi, late Union Minister Murasoli Maran, the Sarkaria Commission, and ED dossiers in recent cases.The situation turned chaotic after Speaker J C D Prabhakar refused to expunge the remarks, ruling that Vijay had merely cited the Sarkaria Commission, which had been discussed at length in the House previously. Declaring that there was no need to expunge the remarks, the Speaker gave his ruling, triggering further escalation as DMK members upped the ante, raised slogans, and brought the proceedings to a standstill by sitting in the well of the House.The Speaker urged the protesting members to return to their seats, offering to allow DMK whip E V Velu and deputy leader of the opposition K N Nehru to speak on the issue. However, the DMK members refused to yield and continued their agitation."I will not reverse my ruling," Speaker Prabhakar asserted before ordering the marshals to remove the unyielding members. He also cautioned Kallakurichi MLA Vasantham K Karthikeyan against approaching the chair.Marshals subsequently entered the House and physically removed the protesting MLAs, carrying out members including Kutty (Valparai), Durai Chandrasekaran (Thiruvaiyaru), Vasantham Karthikeyan (Rishivandiyam) and a few more who refused to budge from the well. The disruption halted assembly proceedings around 10:03 am, following earlier heated exchanges between former ministers Velu and Nehru and ministers Aadhav Arjuna and R Nirmalkumar.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Some can never be happy with India's progress': PM Modi renews 'naraz fufa' jibe at Congress in Vadodara
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday renewed his \"naraz fufa\" jibe at the Congress, saying \"some people could never be happy with India'.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday renewed his "naraz fufa" jibe at the Congress, saying "some people could never be happy with India's progress."The Prime Minister received an enthusiastic welcome at the ‘NaMo for Viksit Bharat’ event, with organisers saying all seats were booked within an hour of online ticket sales opening.The programme featured music and cultural performances, including a rendition of Queen’s ‘We Will Rock You’, as the crowd cheered for the PM.'Where will the trucks go?'Addressing the 'NaMo for Viksit Bharat' event in Vadodara, PM Modi highlighted the capacity of India’s dedicated freight corridors while taking a dig at the Congress by referring them as "naraaz fufa"."Recently, a double-stack container freight train was operated from JNPT (Mumbai) to Vadodara—meaning the train ran with one container stacked on top of another," he said."With this single trip, the volume of cargo transported from Mumbai to Vadodara was equivalent to that of over 250 trucks. Now, enter the 'naraaz fufa' figure—the one who will immediately start complaining: "What about the truck drivers? Where will the trucks go? What will happen to those who bought trucks?" Well, 'fufa' has found something to grumble about now..." he added.PM Modi said the freight corridor would reduce travel time and logistics costs while saving fuel and benefiting the environment.“Today, the work on the 2,800-kilometer corridor has been successfully completed. The Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors are now becoming the backbone of the nation's trade and commerce,” he said.'How country's work culture has transformed?'The Prime Minister also credited his government with speeding up the freight corridor project after 2014, while criticising the previous government for delays."In 2014, the people of Vadodara, Gujarat, and the entire nation sent me from Gujarat to Delhi. The previous government remained in power until 2014; you sent me there, and they were shown the door. In 7-8 years, not even a single kilometer of work on the freight corridor had been completed. Had the country been run according to their methods, who knows—even three or four subsequent generations might have passed without it ever getting done. That was the state in which they had left a project meant to transform India's logistics ecosystem. After 2014, I set about accelerating this work immediately."The Prime Minister said the project had transformed the country's logistics system and reflected a change in work culture."This Dedicated Freight Corridor stands as a testament to how the country's work culture has transformed over the last 12 years. The concept for this Dedicated Freight Corridor was first mooted in 2004... A special company was formed in 2006 to execute this project. Yet, until 2014, the files merely shuttled back and forth; they were just traveling from one table to another. And look at the irony—even these files did not get the benefit of a dedicated corridor..." he added.Event draws huge responseThe ‘NaMo for Viksit Bharat Vadodara’ programme was organised as part of PM Modi's visit to the city, where he inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for various development projects.Gujarat deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi said the programme had received an overwhelming response from residents. For the first time, online ticketing was introduced, with all available seats booked within 60 minutes. Demand was reportedly three times higher than the available capacity.Special fan zones were also set up to accommodate people who could not get seats inside the venue.Ahead of PM Modi’s visit, a ‘Viksit Bharat Padayatra’ was organised on Monday under Sanghavi’s leadership. The march began at the Faculty of Technology in Dandia Bazaar and passed through Kirti Stambh before concluding at Sursagar Lake.A cultural programme was also organised at Sursagar Lake, featuring singer Kailash Kher. ‘Swachhata Doots’ who contributed to keeping Vadodara clean were felicitated during the event.Rs 35,000 crore projects launchedDuring his visit, PM Modi inaugurated, dedicated and laid the foundation stones for development projects worth more than Rs 35,000 crore in Vadodara.A major highlight was the inauguration of three sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC), covering 326 route kilometres and developed at a cost of more than Rs 20,700 crore.The sections connect New Sanand (North) with New Makarpura, New Umbergaon with New Saphale, and New Saphale with New JNPT in Mumbai. The connectivity to Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority is expected to speed up the movement of export-import cargo, improve links between industrial centres and ports and reduce logistics costs.PM Modi also flagged off freight train services from the newly connected sections and a new passenger train between Tanda Road and Vadodara’s Pratapnagar.He dedicated the Jobat-Tanda Road new rail line to the nation. The line, developed as part of the Chhota Udepur-Dhar project, will connect remote and tribal areas of Alirajpur with the national railway network.The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for three railway projects covering 329 km at a cost of more than Rs 9,700 crore, along with three National Highway projects worth around Rs 1,780 crore.Several Gujarat government projects worth around Rs 2,600 crore were also inaugurated or launched, including housing projects under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, a water-supply project for 11 villages in eastern Vadodara, the Vadodara Urban Development Authority Ring Road Phase II and a 110 MW floating solar project at Kadana Dam.Also read: PM Modi opens 326 km of new freight corridor sections, network now completeGet the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2007, Wisconsin used dye to trace why 229 people got sick; septic-tank wastewater reached the drinking well in 6 days, while infiltration-field dye took 15
articles.summary: US News: In June 2007, a severe outbreak of gastroenteritis in Door County, Wisconsin, traced its origins to contaminated well water. Health officials discovered that human waste from a nearby septic system infiltrated the drinking water well, highlighting critical public health and environmental risks in areas with fractured dolomite aquifers.
articles.body: In June 2007, a brand-new restaurant in Door County, Wisconsin, provided the setting for perhaps the most extensively documented outbreak of waterborne disease of recent times in the USA, according to the CDC's Surveillance for Waterborne Disease Outbreaks Associated with Drinking Water, United States, 2007–2008, the MMWR summary covering 2007-2008 outbreaks. According to the same CDC report, 229 cases of acute gastroenteritis occurred among customers and staff at the restaurant not long after it opened, and six people were hospitalized. All this to address the single question of how human waste found its way into a well that complied with all the state building codes.The outbreak: 229 cases, one contaminated wellFirst, a case-control study by Borchardt and colleagues ruled out food poisoning and found that drinking the restaurant's well water was associated with illness (odds ratio = 3.2, a measure of how much more likely illness was in one group versus another). Second, testing detected norovirus genogroup I, a group of viral strains that cause acute gastroenteritis, in the restaurant's well water at around 50 genomic copies per liter. Third, genetic sequencing confirmed the same viral strain, genotype GI.2, in the patients' stool samples, the restaurant's septic tank, and the well water. Together, these findings identify the well as the primary source of infection in the outbreak, as documented by Borchardt and colleagues in the journal Ground Water. The well is 85 meters deep, and the septic system sits 188 meters away, separated from it by a 35-meter-thick soil layer called the vadose zone (the unsaturated ground above the water table).The red dye test revelations In order to determine how the contamination got to the well, two different dyes were injected into two parts of the septic system, the tanks and the infiltration field. Borchardt and colleagues reported that dye injected into the septic tanks reached the well within six days through a leaking fitting, while dye released into the infiltration field took about fifteen days to arrive. This is where the account of wastewater reaching the drinking water well in about a week began. Wastewater from both the tanks and the infiltration field ultimately reached the restaurant's well. This meant the septic effluent was carried by groundwater directly into the drinking water well.Why the Wisconsin Bedrock made this possibleDoor County is located on top of a fractured dolomite aquifer of Silurian age. This rock formation is made up of joints and bedding-plane channels that let water, along with whatever pollutants it carries, move rapidly with little natural filtration. As noted earlier, both the well and the septic system were built entirely in accordance with the state codes in place at the time. Adherence to those codes turned out not to be enough for this particular geology: the setback distances assumed groundwater would move slowly enough to be filtered naturally over weeks or months, but the dye tests showed it could travel through the fractured dolomite in a matter of days.A wider problem across northeastern WisconsinThis is not an isolated case. A related 2021 study by Burch and colleagues, Quantitative Microbial Risk Assessment for Contaminated Private Wells in the Fractured Dolomite Aquifer of Kewaunee County, Wisconsin, examined the same aquifer system in a nearby county, where roughly half the county's population, an estimated 10,000 to 12,000 people, relies on private wells. Using a year-long, countywide pathogen occurrence data set as the input to their quantitative microbial risk model, Burch and colleagues estimated, rather than directly observed, that contaminated private wells could be responsible for as many as 301 modeled cases of acute gastrointestinal illness per year in the county.Of the 301 modeled cases, the study attributed about 230 a year to cattle manure and 12 to human sources. The same study found that Cryptosporidium parvum alone accounted for an estimated 190 of those cases each year, the largest share among the eight pathogens modeled. This pathogen-level figure overlaps with, rather than adds to, the source-level breakdown above (230 bovine, 12 human), since the same modeled illnesses can be counted twice: once by fecal source and once by pathogen. Microbial source tracking allowed the researchers to distinguish bovine from human contamination, an important capability given that the Kewaunee County dolomite aquifer underlies many dairy farms and septic systems.What the findings changedTogether, the two cases have reshaped how experts think about the risks of groundwater contamination in fractured bedrock areas. Inspection of the water supply or proper septic-system design does not eliminate risk. The CDC's national waterborne disease outbreak surveillance report covered the Door County case directly, noting that pathogens reached the water through cracks in the dolomite that created a hydraulic connection between the septic system and the well. The same CDC report found that, among the 36 outbreaks linked to drinking water in 2007 and 2008, 13 of the 21 outbreaks tied to source-water, treatment, or distribution deficiencies were caused by untreated groundwater. The report also noted that EPA regulations do not apply to private wells, and that more than half of the drinking-water outbreaks it reviewed were linked to untreated or inadequately treated groundwater.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: As the 9/11 attacks collapsed his office, a blind man's guide dog helped him down 78 flights to safety and saved his life
articles.summary: US News: September 11, 2026, will mark the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks which collapsed the World Trade Centre and led to the loss of thousands of live.
articles.body: September 11, 2026, will mark the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks which collapsed the World Trade Centre and led to the loss of thousands of lives. It also marks 25 years since Michael Hingson's life was saved by his guide dog, who helped him escape from the 78th story of the north tower of the centre.Hingson, blind since birth, had heard a muffled explosion as he stood in the doorway of his office. "We probably moved about 20 feet," he recalled to PEOPLE. Across the room, his colleague David Frank held onto a desk. “David and I actually said goodbye to each other,” said the 76-year-old, “because we thought we were going to take a 78-floor plunge to the street. Meanwhile, Roselle, Hingson's guide dog, a yellow Labrador retriever, was asleep beneath his desk.Hingson remembered that as the building was righting itself, Frank shouted, “Oh my God, Mike, there’s fire and smoke above us. We got to get out of here — right now.” A regional sales manager for a computer-storage company, Hingson and Frank had been preparing that morning to lead a seminar when a jet hijacked by al-Qaida struck the World Trade Centre at 8:46 am local time.Initially, though, the scale of the terror attack wasn’t clear. Hingson called his wife, Karen, at their home in Westfield, N.J., and told her there had been an emergency. Then he, Roselle and Frank, after a safe sweep of the office and knowing there were no other co-workers there, started retreating down to the ground. Just 15 floors above them, the tower was being consumed in the aftermath of the first plane crash.As the small group made the great escape, Roselle at times walked beside him, guiding him around obstacles. Other times, she walked behind him as he held the railing and climbed down. “The dogs don’t lead,” he explained. “They guide.”As they descended, Hingson repeatedly told Roselle: “Good dog, Roselle. You’re doing a great job.” “I knew she was going to sense the fear in everyone else, so I needed to let her know I was okay,” he said.Not just him, about 10 floors down, a woman behind them stopped and said, "I can't breathe, I can't go on." Hingson turned back to help, offering a hug while Roselle offered some comfort of her own, kisses. By the 50th floor, fear overtook Frank. “Mike, we’re going to die,” he yelled. “We’re not going to make it out of here.” But Hingson was determined.“Stop it, David,” he commanded. “If Roselle and I can go down these stairs, so can you.” The words calmed Frank, who started walking one floor ahead, telling Hingson what he saw as they went further.“Anyone within the sound of his voice heard someone who was calm, focused, going down the stairs and yelling to somebody else that he was okay,” Hingson said. “David had to be one of the major forces keeping people in that stairwell from panicking.”In time, firefighters began passing them on their way up, asking people to just "go down and get out" as they dealt with what was happening upstairs. In total, 343 New York City firefighters died that day when the World Trade Centre towers fell.As Hingson finally reached the lobby, an FBI agent directed him and Frank out of the complex. Soon, the 110-floor south tower was struck by another plane and began disintegrating. Hingson described it as a "rubble that was a combination of a freight train and a waterfall."“The first thing I thought was, ‘God, I can’t believe that you got us out of a building just to have it collapse on us,’” Hingson said. “And when I did that, I literally heard in my head a voice that said, ‘Don’t worry about what you can’t control. Focus on running with Roselle, and the rest will take care of itself.’ ”Out on the streets, Roselle abruptly stopped at the top of a flight of stairs and led Hingson below ground, to shelter in a subway station. When a police officer told them it was safe to leave, Hingson, Roselle and Frank, who had stayed with them, returned to the street and to the shocking sight of the south tower. Or where it should have stood.“David looked at us and said, ‘Oh my God, Mike, all I see are pillars of smoke hundreds of feet tall. It’s gone,’ ” Hingson shared. About 10 minutes later, the building where they had worked and where they had just escaped, the north tower, fell, too.Later that evening, Hingson finally returned home to New Jersey. Soon after the attacks, he moved to California and worked for Guide Dogs for the Blind. He found healing through talking to audiences about trust, teamwork and controlling fear.In 2002, Roselle received the Award for Canine Excellence (ACE) in the service dog category, and at the age of 14, died in June of 2011. Hingson now lives in Victorville, Calif., with Alamo, his ninth guide dog.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: At 10, she lost her grandmother to breast cancer; at 17, Dubai teen Saiyette Aima built an AI platform and took cancer awareness to India
articles.summary: Middle East News: At 10, Saiyette Aima could not understand the medical language around breast cancer. But its consequences were clear to her from the get-go. Her grand.
articles.body: At 10, Saiyette Aima could not understand the medical language around breast cancer. But its consequences were clear to her from the get-go. Her grandmother was diagnosed with Stage 3 disease after noticing a small, pimple-like mark on her neck, she began chemotherapy and radiation and the family quickly entered a period of treatment and uncertainty. While she was thousands of miles away from her grandmother in Delhi, the experience stayed with her. Now, cancer was no longer a disease she read about on paper, it was a part of her life. “I watched her go through chemotherapy and radiation and saw how cancer affected not just her health, but our entire family,” Saiyette told Khaleej Times.Her grandmother later died in 2020, during the Covid-19 pandemic, when travel restrictions made the event even harder for the family. “My parents, my sister and I were the only people in our family that lived here in Dubai. The rest of my family lived with her in Delhi,” she said.Beginning of an effortA few years later, the Dubai College student cut her locks and donated them through Locks of Hope, a Friends of Cancer Patients programme that provides wigs for people undergoing chemotherapy. “Hair loss is such a visible part of treatment for many patients, and it felt like a simple, practical thing I could do,” said the now 17-year-old. “It was a small gesture, but it taught me that I don’t have to wait until I have a large platform or extensive resources to begin helping,” she added. This marked just the beginning of her initiative for bettering the lives of cancer patients.Aima launched For Her, For Hope, a fundraising campaign through YallaGive. While she initially aimed to collect Dh5,000 by approaching her school, family, friends and community, the final amount exceeded Dh10,400 and earned her recognition as YallaGive's Fundraising Hero of the Month. The money supported Pink Caravan, the Friends of Cancer Patients initiative that promotes awareness and offers free screenings.A perceptive and dedicated teenager, Aima soon realised that a single campaign could only help so much. She then created Pink for Purpose, a cancer-awareness initiative.Many people had questions they felt uncomfortable asking and complex medical terminology only made the information difficult to absorb. Thus, she expanded Pink for Purpose into a YouTube channel featuring oncologists and other specialists discussing warning signs, screening, treatment, inherited risks, recovery and the emotional effects of cancer. The conversations also improved her own understanding of the truly life-changing disease. Treatment varies widely among patients; its effects may continue through physical symptoms, and people may also face reduced confidence, fear of recurrence and uncertainty within families. “Cancer can affect almost every part of a person’s life,” she said.Her conversations extended to include educational sessions and magazine content with IntelliJelly, which published her writing and featured an awareness video.Awareness work in IndiaThe most direct phase of her advocacy took her to India, where she helped organise free awareness and screening camps with doctors from AIIMS New Delhi and the National Cancer Institute in Jhajjar. Conversations with 150 attendees exposed her to numerous practical barriers: uncertainty about bodily changes, limited opportunities to ask questions, and health advice obscured by language or terminology. “Giving someone health information is only useful if they can actually understand it and know what to do with it,” she said.CareCheck: An AI platformAll of these experiences and questions transformed into the creation of CareCheck, Aima's proposed AI-powered breast-health platform. It will offer local-language guidance on breast self-awareness, allow users to record concerns, simplify medical information and locate nearby professional care. The platform is designed to guide women through breast self-checks, provide reminders and allow them to record changes and maintain a symptom history. Doctors and healthcare organisations are reviewing its content, wording and safety boundaries.“CareCheck does not diagnose cancer and it does not replace a doctor,” she said. Its purpose is more precise: helping a woman understand a concern, document it and reach appropriate care. She said that the platform is currently being finalised before becoming publicly available.After finishing school, she hoped to study computer science or computer engineering in US or UK, with a particular focus on artificial intelligence. “The emotional ties that I’ve had through cancer have made me realise that I can use CS within the healthcare industry without being a doctor or a nurse,” she said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: After 3 years, Melbourne removed 20,000 love locks from Evan Walker Bridge in 2015; wires were sagging and up to 40,000 keys polluted the Yarra River
articles.summary: US News: Discover how Melbourne's iconic Evan Walker Bridge was impacted by thousands of love locks, leading to their removal and transformation into art. Learn about the romantic trend that became a safety concern, and how the city repurposed the locks into meaningful artworks, preserving the memories of couples while maintaining the bridge's integrity.
articles.body: Couples had been attaching padlocks to the railings of Melbourne's Southgate footbridge for about three years when the city decided the collection had become too heavy. By May 2015, about 20,000 locks covered the bridge's cable railings, and Melbourne City Council said the weight was causing the wires to sag and announced that the locks would be removed.At the time, the bridge was still commonly known as the Southgate footbridge, and was officially renamed the Evan Walker Bridge in July 2015. Couples would write their names or initials on a padlock, attach it to the railing and throw the key into the Yarra River. In Melbourne, the practice had grown quickly enough to create a physical problem for the bridge.The wires began to sagLord Mayor Robert Doyle said the supporting wires were beginning to sag under the accumulated weight. Some locks were being placed across two wires because of the sag, which further complicated the structure. The council estimated that as many as 40,000 keys had been thrown into the Yarra River.The city planned to remove the locks by detaching the support wires and sliding the padlocks off rather than cutting every individual lock from the railing. Officials did not argue that the locks themselves were inherently dangerous; the problem was the accumulated load on infrastructure that had not been designed to carry thousands of additional metal objects. The bridge had become part of a global trend that had also affected bridges in Paris, Cologne and other cities.Twenty thousand locks came downWorkers began removing the locks in May 2015, and the cleanup produced an unusual collection of personal objects. Each lock represented a couple or another personal connection, and many had names or dates engraved into the metal. The council initially asked residents to suggest what should happen to the locks once they had been removed.Some of the discussion centered on recycling or displaying them rather than simply throwing them away, and the eventual solution gave many of them a second life. The City of Melbourne later worked with Craft Victoria on the Love Locks Project, which gave artists the removed padlocks as raw material for new works.The bridge was renamedIn July 2015, the Southgate pedestrian bridge was officially renamed the Evan Walker Bridge in honor of the former Victorian planning minister who was associated with the development of Melbourne's Southbank precinct. The cables still needed to be maintained, and the council continued removing new locks after the large-scale cleanup. A later City of Melbourne collection record describes the removal of almost 20,000 locks as necessary because of safety concerns and damage to the bridge, which had not been designed to carry the additional weight.The locks became artworkArtists were invited to transform the locks into new pieces instead of treating the collection simply as scrap metal, and the resulting works included a large brass sculpture and other objects made from the locks. The transformation also separated the romantic ritual from the bridge itself, since couples could still commemorate their relationships, but the physical act of attaching another lock to the bridge was no longer treated as harmless decoration.Small numbers kept returningPeople continued attaching new padlocks to the bridge, and city workers periodically removed them to protect the structure. By 2018, ABC News reported that new locks were still appearing but were being removed by city officers, and the council said that the continuing removals were intended to preserve the bridge's structural integrity.The original collection became part of the bridge's maintenance history, while the locks that had already been removed were repurposed into artworks. The bridge kept its new name, the Yarra kept the keys that had already been thrown into it, and the 20,000-padlock collection moved from the railing into Melbourne's art and heritage record.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Manipur musician’s death: All 8 accused arrested, strong chargesheet in 2 weeks, says Kiren Rijiju
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju said all eight accused in the alleged killing of 55-year-old Manipuri musician and music teacher Chongtham Vikr.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju said all eight accused in the alleged killing of 55-year-old Manipuri musician and music teacher Chongtham Vikram Singh in Delhi’s Ashram have been arrested.Rijiju said police have assured the family that a strong chargesheet will be filed within two weeks."It is a very sad incident, Vikram Singh from Manipur, who was a musician, he got into altercation with few delivery boys, workers of a 'dhaba', after the fight, he died. I have talked to IGP of South Delhi Range, DCP, Joint CP of Special Police Cell for Northeast. All the eight accused have been arrested. Police also met the family of Vikram Singh. Tomorrow, his body will be taken to Manipur. Police said that within two weeks, a strong chargesheet will be filed in the court, there should be strict punishment, " Rijiju told news agency PTI.Calling the incident “very sad”, Rijiju said Singh had got into an altercation with some delivery boys and workers of a dhaba before he was allegedly beaten and later died during treatment.He said Singh’s body would be taken to Manipur on Wednesday and expressed hope that the accused would face strict punishment.Earlier, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also condemned the alleged mob lynching of Singh, calling it a “chilling reminder” of what he described as “utter lawlessness under the Bharatiya Janata Party” and demanded strict action against those responsible.In a post on X, Kharge wrote, “The merciless lynching of Chongtham Vikram Singh ji, a well-known musician from Manipur, by a mob is yet another chilling reminder of the utter lawlessness under the BJP. Students are unsafe. Women face atrocities every day. People from Northeast India face discrimination. Dalits, Adivasis and minorities remain highly vulnerable."The merciless lynching of Chongtham Vikram Singh ji, a well-known musician from Manipur, by a mob is yet another chilling reminder of the utter lawlessness under the BJP.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Quote of the day by Fyodor Dostoevsky: "Your worst sin is that you have destroyed and…" - a powerful reminder to ask what you are really gaining from every sacrifice
articles.summary: Rest of World News: This line is one of the most quoted passages from Fyodor Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment, and it captures something genuinely powerful about self-be.
articles.body: This line is one of the most quoted passages from Fyodor Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment, and it captures something genuinely powerful about self-betrayal, regret and the choices people make when they lose sight of what actually matters to them. Unlike many quotes about failure that focus on losing money or opportunity, this line points at something considerably more personal, the real damage a person can do to themselves by repeatedly acting against their own values. It is especially relevant in a world where people often feel real pressure to fit in, please others, or simply appear successful. Someone may stay in a situation that genuinely makes them unhappy purely because they fear disappointing another person. Another may quietly give up an ambition simply because it never seemed practical enough to pursue properly, and yet years later they may find that the compromise achieved nothing at all worth having.Quote of the day by Fyodor Dostoevsky"Your worst sin is that you have destroyed and betrayed yourself for nothing"Where this line actually comes fromThe quote comes from Part 4, Chapter 4 of Crime and Punishment, first published in 1866, and it is worth being genuinely accurate about its actual context. The line is not Dostoevsky speaking directly in his own voice. It is dialogue spoken by the character Svidrigaïlov, a genuinely unsettling and morally complicated figure in the novel, to Sonia, a young woman who has been forced into desperate circumstances to support her family. The fuller passage reads, "But you are a great sinner, that's true, and your worst sin is that you have destroyed and betrayed yourself for nothing. Isn't that fearful? Isn't it fearful that you are living in this filth which you loathe so, and at the same time you know yourself that you are not helping any one by it, not saving any one from anything." Dostoevsky, as the author, crafted this scene specifically to explore themes of guilt, sacrifice and self-destruction that run throughout the entire novel, and the line has genuinely outlived its original scene, circulating today as a standalone reflection on self-betrayal more broadly.What is the meaning of Fyodor Dostoevsky’s quoteThe real meaning here lies in the words "destroyed" and "betrayed." This is not describing an ordinary mistake. It describes what happens when someone repeatedly goes against their own conscience or their own values. To genuinely betray yourself can mean knowing exactly what you actually believe while choosing to act differently anyway, out of fear, pressure or simple convenience. It can happen gradually, rather than through one single dramatic decision. Someone may genuinely know that a particular friendship is unhealthy but keep maintaining it because they do not want to be alone. These decisions can feel necessary in the moment, but if they continue for too long, a person can genuinely begin to feel disconnected from who they actually are. The second half of the line, "for nothing," sharpens the whole message. Sacrificing yourself for a genuine purpose is a very different thing from destroying yourself for something that ultimately carries no real value at all.Why this quote still genuinely matters todayModern life creates countless real opportunities for people to compare themselves against each other. Social media and constant professional competition can make it genuinely tempting to change yourself simply to gain approval. People can spend years chasing a career purely because it looks impressive from the outside, even while it genuinely leaves them unhappy. This line encourages a genuinely different kind of self-examination instead. Before making a major compromise, it is worth honestly asking what exactly is being sacrificed, and what is actually being gained in return.The real difference between sacrifice and genuine self-betrayalNot every difficult choice actually means a person is betraying themselves. People regularly make genuine sacrifices for their children, their families or a long-term goal, and the important question is always whether the sacrifice genuinely serves something meaningful. Self-betrayal happens when a person keeps abandoning what actually matters to them without any clear purpose behind it, constantly saying yes when they genuinely want to say no, or giving up an important ambition purely out of fear of other people's opinions. A useful distinction is this: genuine sacrifice should take you somewhere. Self-betrayal can leave you feeling like you have lost yourself without gaining anything real in return.Know what genuinely matters to youPeople can make genuinely poor decisions when they do not have a clear sense of their own values. Knowing what actually matters most makes it considerably easier to recognise when a situation is asking you to compromise too much.Do not confuse approval with genuine happinessBeing accepted by absolutely everyone is genuinely impossible. Constantly changing yourself to satisfy other people can eventually leave you genuinely unsure about what you actually want for yourself.Think honestly about the cost of your choicesEvery major decision genuinely involves a trade-off. Before making a real sacrifice, it helps to consider both sides honestly, asking what you are actually giving up and whether the result is genuinely worth it.Learn to recognise when enough is genuinely enoughPersistence is genuinely valuable, but persistence in the wrong situation can become quietly damaging. Walking away from something that repeatedly harms your sense of self is not always failure. Sometimes it is genuinely self-respect instead.Other famous quotes by Fyodor Dostoevsky"Man only likes to count his troubles; he doesn't calculate his happiness.""Above all, don't lie to yourself. The man who lies to himself and listens to his own lie comes to a point that he cannot distinguish the truth within him, or around him, and so loses all respect for himself.""To go wrong in one's own way is better than to go right in someone else's.""Taking a new step, uttering a new word, is what people fear most."How to apply this quote in daily lifeThis message does not require any dramatic change. It can genuinely begin with small acts of honesty instead. Before agreeing to something, it helps to ask whether you genuinely want to do it, or whether you are simply afraid of disappointing someone else. When considering a career decision, it helps to think beyond salary or prestige and ask whether the work actually fits the life you genuinely want. The same principle applies to relationships too. If you repeatedly have to hide your feelings or pretend to be someone else simply to keep a relationship functioning, it may be worth genuinely examining what that relationship is actually costing you.Why this timeless message still resonatesThis line from Crime and Punishment is ultimately about the genuine value of remaining true to yourself. Life will always involve genuinely difficult decisions and real compromise, and the goal was never to avoid every situation that causes discomfort. The deeper lesson is understanding why you are actually making a sacrifice, and whether it genuinely serves something meaningful. "Your worst sin is that you have destroyed and betrayed yourself for nothing" works as both a warning and a genuine reminder. Before sacrificing an important part of yourself, it helps to pause and ask what you are actually gaining in return.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Built in 1896, the historic five-story St Louis National Cash Register building spans 12,000 sq ft and is up for sale; once listed for $1.4M, it now asks $800,000
articles.summary: News News: ‘The Cosmopolitan’ in St Louis, Missouri, is no ordinary home. Built in 1896, this historic St Louis building once housed the National Cash Register c.
articles.body: ‘The Cosmopolitan’ in St Louis, Missouri, is no ordinary home. Built in 1896, this historic St Louis building once housed the National Cash Register company. Originally built as a place for commerce, the kind of sturdy brick-and-mortar operation that once anchored downtown, the property is now up for sale, according to Realtor.com.The five-story structure is now listed for $800,000, nearly half of its initial asking price of $1.4 million, in less than four years. That's $75 per square foot for a 12,000-square-foot Gothic Revival building in downtown. The buyer is not merely investing in an ordinary house, but an enormous historic building that looks and feels like an art museum, and they get to live and work in it.Historic five-story buildingThe St Louis historic building has had many owners before finally being listed again. After National Cash Register’s tenure, the building became a showroom for Clark Peeper furniture. Then came the interior designers Mark and Mary Pitliangas, who saw something in the bones that others might have overlooked. Not a fixer-upper, but a canvas. Known for their artistic endeavours, they had also restored a retro landmark in the form of a 25.5-foot-tall Vess Soda Bottle.What they built inside this building is almost impossible to describe without walking through it. The first floor is a Gothic lounge that feels pulled from another century. The travertine floors, custom stone and tilework, and illuminated stained glass run throughout the building. There are ceiling murals. There's a fireplace that was rescued from somewhere else and given new purpose here. The couple selected high-end antiques for features ranging from lighting to wall treatments, including a bar they retrofitted from an antique Chicago piece. And the best part? A brass elevator connects the five-story building.Five floors with numerous possibilitiesThe buyer is not getting an ordinary building. In fact, this historic building can transform into almost anything. Each level is curated differently. Every floor is fully zoned for both commercial and residential activities, which means buyers aren't locked into a single vision. The mezzanine functions as office and meeting space. The third floor holds a residential loft. The fourth could be a studio, storage, or a gallery. The penthouse is, of course, unlike anything. It features travertine floors, illuminated stained glass, ceiling buttresses, and modern amenities including Viking appliances and a home theatre.This historic building is not a cash register factory or a furniture store anymore. It is ready to become anything you want. The 12,000 sq ft building can be a private residence, an office building, or both.Treasure trove for antiquesThe building is a treasure trove for antiques, including custom tile, glasswork, and hand-painted artwork. Even the ceilings are embellished. Much of the furniture and antiques were either made or purchased specifically for The Cosmopolitan and will stay with the property. Some pieces are sentimental to the Pitliangases. Others are inventory from their design business, Antique Architectural Decor, which sources and installs custom materials for clients across the country. This is a bonus for buyers. You're not just purchasing walls and floors, but inheriting a curated collection of unique art pieces.The building has been on the market since 2022. Over the years, the price has fluctuated depending on market trends. Initially, The Cosmopolitan was listed for $1.4 million, but they didn’t really find any buyers. So they lowered the price. Now the asking price is $800,000, which means the price per square foot is roughly $100 less than the current Missouri average.“The ideal buyer is someone with flair and a desire to create unique experiences—whether that’s short-term rentals, creative offices, artist spaces, or the most singular home in the city,” previous listing agent Justin Ströhm told the outlet when the property first hit the market.No one is pretending that The Cosmopolitan is a starter property or an investment flip. But it's a statement. It’s an extraordinary building, so, of course, the buyers should match the vibe. They should understand that maintaining Gothic Revival architecture, custom tilework, and a brass elevator requires the kind of obsessive attention the Pitliangases had for the past two decades. The right person will see the 130-year-old building for what it is.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.
